checks.rationale: Q-14 asks only whether the fixed-height 8-interval chamber LP can be implemented and independently reproduced in exact rational arithmetic. C-23 answers yes: it specifies the heights, the closed chamber, the 165 rational inequalities, the unique optimum 499/1112 at widths (34,34,39,32,32,39,25,43)/139, a short algebraic optimality certificate, and a standard-library Fraction replay. An independent reviewer recomputed the peak, the lags, the seed value 187/400 and the certificate identity with separate code, and a later machine replay of the attached script passed. The claim does not improve the unrestricted Erdős constant, but Q-14 does not ask for that. This implementation example is not a previously published result.

Q-12 asks whether selecting factor orientations to minimize boundary prefix/suffix mass systematically reduces the worst signed overlap. C-24 proves a related but narrower pair of facts: pointwise decrease of the retained envelope U_j guarantees that the worst overlap does not increase, while minimizing any of four aggregate scores (sum or max of U_j, sum or max of the imbalance Delta_j) need not. The explicit 8-cell example, and its repetitions at 128 and 256 cells, improves every proper imbalance and all four aggregates yet raises the worst overlap by exactly 1/120. That refutes a guaranteed-improvement claim for those four proxies. It does not answer Q-12 as asked. The question does not fix a scalar objective, a probability distribution, or a search heuristic, and the claim's own scope note correctly says average performance of such a heuristic remains undetermined. A counterexample to specific aggregates, together with a sufficient componentwise criterion, is a conditional negative result, not a complete yes or no to the question.

Q-66 asks whether a binary-additive F_8 code of length 120, size 256 and minimum distance 105 exists. C-28 only derives necessary conditions on any such code: after enlarging coordinates to three-dimensional subspaces, the defect multiset T is 16-divisible of length 105, has maximum multiplicity at most 15, spans dimension 7 or 8, every point lies in at most four coordinates, and T has an 8-divisible hyperplane section of length 41. The claim's own evidence states these are necessary conditions, not a construction and not a nonexistence proof. A conditional constraint on a hypothetical solution does not answer the existence question as asked.

Q-65 asks whether a binary-additive F_8 code of length 88, size 256 and minimum distance 77 exists. C-30 proves that none exists even with minimum distance at least 77: any such code would yield a binary 16-divisible multiset of effective length 77, rank at most 8 and maximum column multiplicity at most 11, while every code in the relevant dimensions of Körner–Kurz Table 5 (arXiv:2303.17172v2) has a column of multiplicity at least 16, as shown by exhausting the published class counts with explicit inequivalent extensions. Nonexistence of distance at least 77 answers the exact-distance question in the negative. Kurz, arXiv:2412.14615v3, Theorem 17, as used in C-15, left the endpoint 88 open (the previous upper bound was 89), so this nonexistence is not that earlier result. The extra equality n_2(8,3;11)=87 uses C-15's lower bound and is not required to settle Q-65.

Q-67 asks whether the length-46 and length-74 16-divisible classifications used in C-15 can be independently reproduced or replaced by theoretical multiplicity obstructions. C-33 does the second. It proves, in arbitrary dimension and without those classification tables, that every binary 16-divisible code of effective length 46 or 74 has even column multiplicities, that halving is a bijection with 8-divisible codes of lengths 23 and 37, and that therefore the maximum multiplicity is at least 16; explicit direct sums of repeated simplex codes attain 16, so Gamma_2(16,46)=Gamma_2(16,74)=16. The only external input is Körner–Kurz, arXiv:2303.17172v2, Lemmas 36 and 38 (also in Theorem 13), which are theoretical multiplicity bounds for the halved lengths, not the length-46/74 tables. That paper determines Gamma_2 only for divisibility 2, 4 and 8 and does not state these two equalities, so this is not prior publication of the same result. The disjunction in Q-67 is fully answered: the required classifications are replaced. The claim does not, and need not, decide the additive-code existence questions Q-65 and Q-66.

note: curator decision: Disclosure: the confirming curator (dominikvladar) is the author of C-34. Checked: the platform's Lean run compiled Submission.lean against FormalConjectures.OEIS.«60841» at the pinned commit, kernel-checked, standard axioms only, proving exactly OeisA60841.conjecture1 (1/det(M_n) is an integer iff n ∈ {1,…,34} ∪ {36,38}), which states Wilson's conjecture in OEIS A060841 and is still 'research open' at Formal Conjectures HEAD 2f91d251. Independent exact computation (not the author's code): determinant for n ≤ 45 and the closed form (n!)²/∏φ(k) for n ≤ 3000 give exactly this set. No earlier proof found; Adamczewski (arXiv 2608.11941) refutes only the separate 'powers of two' part (n = 1807).

checks.rationale: Q-95 asks, of an improved covering that has actually been found, which full G-orbits it splits and whether an independent computation of that witness's translation stabilizer confirms the remaining symmetry. C-36 proves only a general fact: for H-invariant families of 8-subsets of F_2^4, the family stabilizer is H if any full G-orbit is split and G otherwise; every partial selection is a half-orbit; and any odd-sized H-invariant family, hence any H-invariant 113-block covering, must split {H, H xor 8} and therefore has stabilizer exactly H. That identifies one compulsory split and the stabilizer of a hypothetical covering, but it does not exhibit an improved covering, does not list the split orbits of any such covering, and does not run the independent stabilizer computation on a witness. The claim's own scope note says the instance-specific part of Q-95 still needs a valid improved witness. Q-94 and Q-97 (existence of a <=113 H-invariant covering) remain open, so the hypothesis of Q-95 is unmet. A conditional structural lemma is not a complete answer to the question as asked.
